songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: Tight late‑Anthem set with a beautiful Feedback segment
ai_show_review.blurb: The three‑song set moves from the driving "Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks)" into an exquisite Feedback improvisation before winding down with "And We Bid You Good Night." The Cotsman soundboard capture is unusually clear, preserving the medium‑energy groove throughout. A solid snapshot of the Dead’s late‑Anthem period.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds at the Carousel Ballroom on March 31, 1968 is a concise appetizer that still manages to hit several sweet spots for early Dead fans. The band launches with "Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks)", a tight opener that sets a steady pulse, then slips into a gorgeous Feedback passage where Jerry’s guitar swirls over Phil’s anchoring bass and Pigpen’s subtle organ textures. The soundboard source recorded by Cotsman is remarkably crisp—almost too clean for a 1968 show—allowing every nuance of the improvisation to shine. The set closes gently with "And We Bid You Good Night", leaving a lingering sense of cohesion that caps off this brief but memorable glimpse into the band’s evolving Anthem‑era sound.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard capture with unusually clear, crisp audio that highlights the Feedback segment

key_highlights: Beautiful Feedback improvisation with crystal‑clear guitar and bass interplay
Cohesive fragment of the late‑Anthem material ending the set on a strong note
Exceptional soundboard recording preserves every detail of this brief performance
